To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the geometry of artery, porosity of its tissues, and the initial location of particles are decisive factors in the MDT efficacy; (ii) the MDT efficacy increases by increasing the particles/drugs/cargo size, MFS, and the relative permeability of particles; and (iii) the MDT in healthy artery shows more particles retention in the tissue than diseased one.

the MDT is a promising approach for cancer and artery diseases therapy, and the magnetic particle penetration into the artery layers and the inflamed part is highly affected by magnetic field strength, particle size and the initial position of the particles.
the MDT in artery tissue and its fibrous cap is a potential treatment for artery diseases such as artery atherosclerosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new computational method for the design, analysis, and optimization of MDT for arterial diseases and cancer treatments.
the design, development, and optimization of MDT in the artery flow.
the design of a new magnetic-based drug/cargodelivery system for the delivery of drugs and/or drug-loaded nanoparticles into arteries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MDT is a promising approach for drug delivery in arteries.
magnetic approaches can be used for the treatment of arterial diseases and cancer.
the MDT is a promising approach for the targeted delivery of drug/cargo to the arterial flow and diseased artery.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MDT is a promising method for drug delivery in arteries.
the MDT can be used for drug delivery in artery flow.
the magnetic field strength, the particle size, and the magnet size are the most effective factors for magnetic drug delivery.
The main takeaway from our work is that
magnetic drug delivery is a promising technique for drug delivery to the artery wall and atherosclerotic plaque.
the MDT in the artery is a promising method, but its efficacy is highly dependent on the particle size and MFS.
the magnetic drug targeting in the artery tissue is a promising method for the treatment of cancer and arterial diseases.
